summary.headline: A top-quality bank, priced a little ahead of its value
summary.text: Commercial Bank of Ceylon (COMB.N0000 voting, COMB.X0000 non-voting) is Sri Lanka's largest private bank, with Rs 3.74tn of assets and a Bangladesh operation. It is a strong bank: return on equity 20% (first half of 2026), net interest margin 4.5%, a 38% cost-to-income ratio, CET1 capital 13.2% against an 8.5% minimum, and a Rs 10.50 dividend for 2025. At Rs 224.75 (CSE, 11 November 2026) it trades at 1.04x its group NAV of Rs 216.14 and 5.7x trailing earnings. Four methods put fair value at about Rs 182, so the voting share is about 23% above it; the non-voting share (Rs 195.50, same dividends) is about 7% above. I'd buy at up to Rs 154.70 and treat under Rs 136.50 as a strong buy. Watch impairments: second-quarter charges nearly tripled to Rs 11.7bn, which the bank linked to the geopolitical environment, and gross Stage 3 loans are still 5.3%.

quality.reason: High returns, sound capital, profitable through the crisis and a steady dividend.

tests.label: Return on equity of 15% or more
Steady profit: no loss in five years, no one-offs
tests.note: Profit dipped in 2023 (ROE 9.8%) during the debt restructuring; 2024 included restructuring one-offs.

tests.label: Profit turns into cash and dividends
tests.note: Rs 10.50 for 2025 (Rs 8.00 cash + Rs 2.50 in shares); about 29% of profit paid out.

valuation.note: Fair value weights the bear/base/bull averages of four methods 30/50/20 (about 0.84x group NAV). The same levels apply to both share classes.

dividend.label: for 2025 (Rs 8.00 cash + Rs 2.50 in new shares)

highlights.title: First half of 2026
highlights.text: Group profit up 13.7% to Rs 35.4bn (EPS Rs 21.14 against Rs 18.87). Net interest income up 15.8% to Rs 79.7bn; total operating income up 17.9%. ROE 20.3%, NIM 4.51%, cost-to-income 37.8%.

highlights.title: Impairments jumped in the second quarter
highlights.text: Impairment charges were Rs 11.7bn in April–June against Rs 4.0bn a year earlier (Rs 14.8bn for the half, up 33%), which the bank linked to the geopolitical environment. Second-quarter profit still rose 8%.
Group profit Rs 60.9bn (up 9%), EPS Rs 36.86. Gross loans up 37% to Rs 2.09tn. Dividend Rs 10.50 (Rs 8.00 cash, Rs 2.50 scrip). Net Stage 3 ratio fell to 1.54% from 2.76%.

highlights.title: Capital
highlights.text: CET1 13.2% and total capital 16.6% at June 2026, down from 14.2% and 18.1% at end-2024 as loans grew fast; still well above minimums.

models.name: Justified price to book
models.comment: Book value Rs 216.14 × (ROE − growth) ÷ (cost of equity − growth): ROE 15% / 17% / 19%.

models.name: Dividend model
models.comment: Rs 10.50 / 11.50 / 12.50 a share, growing 4% / 7% / 9% for five years, then 5% / 6% / 7%.

models.name: Residual income
models.comment: ROE moving from 20% to 15% / 17% / 19% over ten years; 29% payout.

modelsNote: A bank's cash flows are mostly lending and deposits, so instead of a cash-flow DCF I used residual income and a justified price-to-book, alongside P/E and dividends (same approach as Sampath and HNB).

scenarios.common: 10-year government bond about 12.4% (9 Nov 2026) plus a premium for a leveraged bank with large government-bond holdings. Base 2026 EPS assumes a second half similar to the first, less higher impairments.

sensitivity.title: Residual income base case, Rs per share
sensitivity.note: Today's Rs 224.75 needs a long-run ROE near 18% at an 18% cost of equity, or a 16.5% cost of equity.

buyPlan.note: About Rs 80,080 in total, against Rs 112,375 at Rs 224.75. Prices apply to either share class.
buyPlan.realism: Rs 154.70 is below the 12-month lows (voting Rs 170, non-voting Rs 176), so it needs a broad market fall. The non-voting share (Rs 195.50) is the cheaper way in.

higher: ROE holding at 20% with impairments easing.
Interest rates falling (each point off the cost of equity adds roughly Rs 25–30 a share).
lower: Capital ratios falling further with loan growth (a rights issue would dilute).
Higher bank taxes or another sovereign debt event.

notes.disclaimer: These are estimates from the 2023–2025 annual reports and the interim reports to June 2026. The September 2026 quarter wasn't in the folder. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.

Decision box.Verdict: Overpriced: voting share about 23% above fair value of Rs 182; non-voting about 7% above.
Decision box.Expected yearly return at Rs 224.75: About 10% a year: dividend 4.7% + book growth about 12% − about 7% a year if the price moved to fair value.
Decision box.Confidence: Medium to high: a strong bank; impairments and capital are the uncertainties.
Decision box.Margin of safety: Buy 15% below fair value (Rs 154.70), strong buy 25% below (Rs 136.50).

Business and moat.What it does: Sri Lanka's largest private commercial bank: corporate, SME and retail banking, 272 branches in Sri Lanka and 20 in Bangladesh, plus a small Maldives operation.
Business and moat.Moat: Wide: scale, low-cost deposits (Rs 3.0tn), the highest capital base among private banks, strong brand.

Management and governance.Ownership: Widely held: Y.S.H.I. Silva 9.9%, D.P. Pieris 9.6%, DFCC Bank 9.6%, EPF 7.3%, IFC 7.1%, Sri Lanka Insurance 5.0%.

Sri Lanka checks.Interest rates: Watch: policy rate 8.75%; bond yields about 12.4%.
Sri Lanka checks.Sovereign exposure: Risk: large government-securities holdings; the 2022–2024 restructuring cut profits.

Investment case and sell rules.Why own it: Top-quality bank with 20% ROE and a 4–5% yield, best bought below book.
Investment case and sell rules.Sell triggers: Price more than 30% above fair value (above Rs 236.60); CET1 below 11%; ROE below 15% for a year.

What this analysis doesn't cover: The September 2026 quarter (not in the folder).

Four methods put fair value at about Rs 182, so the voting share is about 23% above it; the non-voting share (Rs 195.50, same dividends) is about 7% above. Method | Bear | Base | Bull | Weighted
